rationale: Kept from the revision: the sensor layout (five sensors at x = -0.024 to +0.024 m, 12 mm footprints) covers the 25 mm tape, and the antisymmetric weights (-1.5, -0.75, 0, 0.75, 1.5) give the correct steering sign. Geometry, weights and last_direction line-loss handling are unchanged. kp stays at 3.5 and kd at 0.01 (small damper, no large derivative kick on edge transitions), as in the revision. base_speed stays at 1.9 for margin against the 3 s limit; the speed is still unverified against real ground speed. Changed: ki reduced from 0.2 to 0.1. The critique's windup point is valid: on sustained bends the integral sits near its +/-2 clamp and holds a drift of up to 0.2 turn units (about 70 PWM) after the bend, and the fixed motor mismatch is small (about 2 percent), so a lower ki is enough. Partly rejected: I did not lower base_speed or raise kp to resolve the speed-versus-control trade-off, because there is no telemetry yet to show which one wins; the next round should decide it from data. Decision rules for the next round: if steering_oscillation or max_error is high on the slalom, reduce kp first, then kd; if completion is 0 with progress well below 1 and completion_time near 3 s, raise base_speed; if line_loss_events is above zero on the slalom, reduce base_speed before changing the gains. Expected result: completion on oval and s-bend with lower jitter than the draft; the slalom remains the main risk, and these values are estimates until telemetry exists.
